title: Max Newman
name: Max Newman
summary: British mathematician who led Bletchley Park’s Newmanry and helped establish the operational context for Colossus-assisted cryptanalysis.
whyThisMatters: Newman helped connect mathematical cryptanalysis to automated computation. The Newmanry’s work against Lorenz traffic is a key chapter in the co-evolution of security analysis and programmable electronic computing.

sections.overview:
Max Newman was a British mathematician and cryptanalyst. At Bletchley Park he led the section later called the Newmanry, which developed mechanised methods for attacking Lorenz-encrypted German messages.

Computing in cryptanalysis

Newman’s group defined a demanding cryptanalytic problem and worked with engineers including Tommy Flowers to automate parts of its solution. The resulting Colossus machines were used operationally during the war.

In memoriam

Newman died in 1984. His academic and wartime work helped shape the early history of computing.

timeline.event: Becomes a professor at the University of Manchester.
Leads a Bletchley Park section attacking Lorenz traffic.
Supports development of electronic methods that lead to Colossus.
Founds the Royal Society Computing Machine Laboratory at Manchester.
